newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private network RTL posts record ad sales.
newsitem.headline: German private network RTL posts record ad sales.

text.p: Top German private television network RTL said on Thursday its advertising turnover had for the first time surpassed three billion marks and it predicted a robust 1997.
The station posted 3.211 billion marks in advertising sales in 1996, up from 2.873 billion marks the previous year. Net advertising proceeds grew by 4.7 percent to 2.052 billion marks, RTL said.
The company also announced a boost in profits to 144.1 million marks from 102.6 million marks in 1995, with growth in both its licensing revenues and sponsoring business.
RTL said it has led the German television market in ratings since 1993 and ranks as Europe's leader in advertising income.

Network general manager Helmut Thoma told a conference of industries that advertise that RTL and ProSieben were the only two profitable stations in Germany, due largely to over-regulation and a saturated market.
The station said its expansion to a 30 percent advertising market share in Germany, along with its plans to invest more in programming, should pave the way for more growth in 1997.

RTL announced last month it plans to spend 1.12 billion marks for in-house and purchased programming, 700 million marks of which will go to deals with independent German film and television production houses.
RTL is a unit of Europe's largest broadcasting group, CLT-UFA, whose largest shareholders are media giant Bertelsmann and Luxembourg holding company Audiofina.
